doc: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project)
title: Prompt Injection
summary: User or content-supplied prompts alter the behaviour or output of the model in unintended ways, including through indirect content the model ingests.
note: Identifier and title verified 2026-09-10 against genai.owasp.org; the 2025 list was published on 17 November 2024. Descriptions are paraphrased. Superseded 2026-09-16 by the 2026 edition entry OWASP:LLMTop10-2026:LLM01; kept because rule packs and golden-set fixtures cite the 2025 id.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project)
title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
summary: The model or application exposes sensitive information, such as personal data, credentials or proprietary content, through its outputs or context.
note: Identifier and title verified 2026-09-10 against genai.owasp.org; the 2025 list was published on 17 November 2024. Descriptions are paraphrased. Superseded 2026-09-16 by the 2026 edition entry OWASP:LLMTop10-2026:LLM02; kept because rule packs and golden-set fixtures cite the 2025 id.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Agent Goal Hijack
summary: Attackers manipulate an agent's objectives, task selection or decision pathways through prompt-based manipulation, deceptive tool outputs, malicious artefacts or forged agent-to-agent messages, because agents cannot reliably separate instructions from content.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Tool Misuse
summary: An agent applies legitimate tools in unsafe or unintended ways — through prompt injection, misalignment, unsafe delegation or ambiguous instructions — leading to data exfiltration, manipulated tool output or workflow hijacking.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted. Title reconciled 2026-09-16 against the OWASP Gen AI Security Project announcement of 9 December 2025, which is the canonical short form; the longer form previously held here came from pre-release material. Previous form: "Tool Misuse and Exploitation".

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Identity & Privilege Abuse
summary: Dynamic trust and delegation between agents are exploited to escalate access, hijack privileges or act without attribution, because agents often lack a distinct governed identity of their own.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted. Title reconciled 2026-09-16 against the OWASP Gen AI Security Project announcement of 9 December 2025, which is the canonical short form; the longer form previously held here came from pre-release material. Previous form: "Identity and Privilege Abuse".

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
summary: Agents, tools, models, datasets, registries and agentic interfaces such as MCP or A2A come from third parties and may be malicious, compromised or tampered with, including components composed at runtime.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Unexpected Code Execution
summary: Code-generation features or embedded tool access are exploited so that generated or injected code executes on hosts or in containers, bypassing controls designed for ordinary tool use.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted. Title reconciled 2026-09-16 against the OWASP Gen AI Security Project announcement of 9 December 2025, which is the canonical short form; the longer form previously held here came from pre-release material. Previous form: "Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)".

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Memory & Context Poisoning
summary: Adversaries corrupt or seed an agent's stored or retrieved context — memory, summaries, embeddings or RAG stores — so that later reasoning, planning or tool use becomes biased or unsafe.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
summary: Messages between autonomous agents lack authentication, integrity, confidentiality or semantic validation, allowing interception, spoofing or manipulation of agent intents across transport, routing and discovery layers.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Cascading Failures
summary: A single fault such as a hallucination, malicious input, corrupted tool or poisoned memory propagates across autonomous agents and compounds into system-wide harm.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
summary: The trust that users place in fluent, apparently expert agents is exploited to influence decisions, extract information or obtain approval for actions without independent validation.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project, Agentic Security Initiative)
title: Rogue Agents
summary: Malicious or compromised agents deviate from their intended function or authorised scope and act harmfully or deceptively, with loss of behavioural integrity and governance after the drift begins.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official PDF (Version 2026, December 2025) downloaded from genai.owasp.org; the document is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is paraphrased here, not quoted.

doc: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0
title: Encoding and Sanitization
summary: Requirements for output encoding, escaping and sanitisation so that untrusted content cannot be interpreted as code or commands by interpreters and downstream components.

doc: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project)
title: Prompt Injection
summary: User- or content-supplied input steers the model away from its intended behaviour, including through indirect content the model ingests. Design time can only evidence the mitigating structure — isolation of untrusted input, a content-safety component, an output-handling step — never the absence of the flaw.
